findings.quote: Confusing the very short range of the weak nuclear force with the strong nuclear force gives 10⁻¹⁸ m.
findings.note: At this syllabus level the range quoted for the weak nuclear force is 10⁻¹⁶ m, which is printed here as option 2 — the same value the 2025 paper in this chapter treats as the answer to 'the range of weak nuclear force'. So the weak-force confusion leads a student to option 2, not to option 1; the entry points at the wrong option. (10⁻¹⁸ m is the W-boson range used in particle physics, not a value in this course.)
findings.fix: Confusing the range of the weak nuclear force, about 10⁻¹⁶ m, with the range of the strong nuclear force gives 10⁻¹⁶ m — this entry should point at option 2.

notes: Solved independently: the strong nuclear force acts only over nuclear dimensions and falls to zero beyond a few femtometres, so its range is of the order 10⁻¹⁵ m. Option 3. Both step equations are true as written. common_mistakes[0] (option 4, exponent −13 instead of −15) is correct, including the claim that this is two orders of magnitude too large.
